name: Lazarus RipDoc Augmentation Surgical Full Rig
description:
A complete street-clinic augmentation surgeon's kit: antimicrobial slate-teal scrub top and drawstring trousers in fluid-resistant BioWeave, a knee-length sterile apron with magnetic tool-strip across the chest, nitrile-grip gloves with haptic feedback pads at the fingertips, and low-profile closed-toe clogs with puncture-resistant soles. A lightweight magnifying visor flips up from a padded headband, and a rear neck pocket holds a sterile BCI tap tool.

The apron's chest strip holds scalpels, neural probes, and chrome calibration wands via magnet. Everything is bleach-rated and designed for fast decontam between patients.
functionality: Fluid-repellent BioWeave resists blood and coolant splash, magnetic tool-strip for surgical instrument retention, haptic fingertip pads for precision chrome calibration, flip-up magnifying visor for neural port work, BCI tap tool pocket.
what_it_says: They fix what hospitals won't touch, for people hospitals won't see.
story_hooks: The apron's magnetic strip has a custom slot for a piece of military-grade chrome that isn't sold commercially — and the doc won't say where they got it.
The haptic gloves are logged to a stolen BCI calibration license, meaning every surgery technically belongs to a Tier 4 hospital upspire.
A patient's chrome arm left trace coolant on the apron that matches a rare military-grade fluid — someone powerful came through this clinic recently.
